model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, retention on common equity

inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-EQUIVALENTS, not ordinary shares. Ordinary shares outstanding 2,484.58m at 2026-03-31 (20-F FY2026, ex-treasury; issued 2,489.85m), less ~24.35m repurchased under the JPY200bn programme completed 2026-09-18 (cancellation 2026-10-23) = 2,460.2m; dilutive share-based awards only 0.39m (20-F EPS note), ignored. Divided by 0.2 because 1 ADS = 0.2 ordinary share (ratio changed from 1 ADS = 2 shares at the October 2020 1-for-10 share consolidation) -> 12,301m ADS-equivalents. Held flat: buybacks are a use of the FCFE already being valued, not extra value.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market treatment: Mizuho's executive stock compensation runs through a BIP/stock-delivery trust that buys shares in the market and is expensed inside G&A; no ShareBasedCompensation tag in the 20-F XBRL and dilutive awards are 0.39m shares (0.02%). Charged inside the margin, so house and street coincide.
inputs.fcf_definition: Bank FCFE, not owner FCF. last_fcf = FY3/26 shareholder distributions actually paid: common dividends JPY368.7bn + buybacks JPY404.3bn (20-F cash flow statement) = JPY773bn, ~62% of J-GAAP profit attributable of ~JPY1,249bn. Forward FCFE = J-GAAP-calibrated profit to common less the equity retention needed to grow book with risk-weighted assets. Interest income is the bank's revenue, not excess-cash income, so interest_income = 0.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts JPY (model) to USD (quote): 1/157.83 = 0.0063359, Yahoo Finance JPY=X 157.83 at 2026-10-03T21:07Z. Per-share values are per ADS-equivalent (0.2 ordinary share), so intrinsic_value is USD per MFG ADS, comparable to current_price; the *_jpy twins are JPY per ADS; JPY per ordinary share = *_jpy x 5. Parity check: Tokyo 8411.T close JPY8,446 on 2026-10-02 x 0.2 / 157.83 = US$10.70 vs the NYSE MFG close at price_as_of (ADR ~1.8% above local, mostly the later US close); a 1:2 ratio would imply US$107.
inputs.fy0: FY2026 (year ended 2026-03-31; Mizuho calls it FY2025)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single JPY cost of equity 9.0% across all scenarios (risk charged once, via scenario weights). Built in the flows' own currency: JGB 10-year ~2.0-2.3% (assumption; not fetched — BOJ policy rate ~0.75%) + beta ~1.1-1.2 to TOPIX x Japan ERP ~5.5-6.0% = ~8.5-9.2%. Megabanks' own disclosed cost-of-capital assumptions sit around 8-9%. A USD rate (UST 10Y 5.28% at price_as_of) would overcharge the JPY flows by the rate differential.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: rent (operating lease cost JPY103bn) sits inside G&A/occupancy, i.e. inside pre-tax profit. lease_cost_pct_path = 0, no lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the flow: the margin is calibrated to J-GAAP profit attributable to owners of parent. US GAAP NI to NCI (JPY168bn FY26) is dominated by consolidated VIEs/funds and is not in the J-GAAP figure. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.gaap_note: The 20-F is US GAAP; guidance, dividends (40% payout policy) and the medium-term plan are J-GAAP. US GAAP NI to MHFG FY26 was JPY1,158bn but includes JPY1,036bn pre-tax equity-securities fair-value gains offset by JPY-713bn derivative and JPY-386bn unrealised FX losses (FY25 US GAAP JPY593bn vs J-GAAP ~JPY885bn) — too noisy to anchor. Flows therefore use J-GAAP profit attributable: FY3/26 ~JPY1,249bn (implied by the raised FY3/27 guidance of JPY1,400bn being +12.1% YoY, per Analysis.json; not read from a Tanshin), FY3/27 guidance JPY1,400bn. base_revenue JPY3,469bn = US GAAP net interest income 1,686.5 + noninterest income 2,818.1 - equity-securities FV gains 1,035.6; it is a scaling device for the margin, and FY0 margin 49.3% = 1,249 / (1-27%) / 3,469.
inputs.data_quality_warning: core_metrics/CSV labels every period 'USD' but the values are JPY (XBRL hardcoded-USD bug, same as HDB/BILI); CSV NetIncome FY2026 1,326,013 is NI incl. NCI (attributable is 1,158,031); CSV Revenue is gross (interest + noninterest income), which doubled FY23->FY24 on overseas rates; pre-FY2020 EPS/shares are pre-consolidation. sanity_check.py multiples for MFG should not be trusted without a manual JPY-per-share recheck.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (HDB, IBN, HSBC, BMO, USB, WFC). No prior MFG valuation and no MEMORY.md entry. Engine mapping: revenue = net revenue ex equity FV gains; 'ebitda' = J-GAAP-calibrated pre-tax profit to common (after credit costs, depreciation, NCI); da_pct 0 (depreciation already inside pre-tax profit, IT/branch capex treated as maintenance funded within it); tax 27% (J-GAAP effective; statutory 30.6%; US GAAP FY26 effective 21.3%, cash tax paid JPY276bn); 'capex' = equity retention. Net debt 0: deposits, repos and JPY20.8tn long-term debt are operating funding. Equity bridge deducts the JPY200bn buyback paid after the balance-sheet date (it was a distribution of the Y1 flow already counted). Implied multiples at the weighted value are checked by hand in JPY per ordinary share against book value/share ~JPY4,580 (11,478 - 200 / 2,460m).

equity_bridge.item: Buyback paid May-Sep 2026 (after 2026-03-31 balance sheet), distributed out of the Y1 FCFE
equity_bridge.note: JPY200bn programme completed 2026-09-18, ~24.35m shares; shares already reduced

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.4% vs EPS 15.2% and CSV revenue 20.2%: revenue is gross interest+noninterest income (inflated by overseas rates, not a growth measure) and US GAAP EPS swings with equity-securities fair value (FY23 -5.52). Book growth is held down by 55-65% payouts. Not used to drive the projection.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs to FY2026 (year to 2026-03-31) from MFG_Metrics.csv (US GAAP, JPY despite the USD label). FCF CAGRs not meaningful for a bank (OCF swings by trillions with trading/deposit flows). EPS 3yr undefined (negative base).

base.capex_rationale: Equity retention, not capex: prior-year common book x balance-sheet (RWA) growth for the year, expressed as % of that year's net revenue; book opens at JPY11,478bn (US GAAP total MHFG shareholders' equity 2026-03-31) and grows only by retention, so terminal-year retention equals book x terminal growth.
base.terminal_note: Gordon growth governs (FCFE multiple 1+g over CoE-g = 13.5x bear, 14.6x base, 15.8x bull); the 16x cap is set above all three so it does not bind. A 12x cap would have silently cut the base TV ~18%.
base.narrative: FY3/27 profit attributable to owners of parent at the raised guidance of JPY1.40tn (+12.1%), from net-revenue growth of ~9% on BOJ normalisation (policy rate ~0.75%) and the US CIB/fee build, with mild operating leverage. Margin edges up to the medium-term-plan level (ROE >12%, net business profit JPY1.8-2.0tn by FY3/29) then gives back half a point as credit costs normalise from benign levels. Risk-weighted assets / tangible capital grow 4% a year near term (overseas loans, Greenhill-led IB) fading to 2%; everything else is paid out, so total payout rises from ~67% to ~84% as growth slows. Steady-state ROE ~12.5% against a 9% CoE = ~1.5x book.

bull.narrative: Guidance is beaten again (Q1 FY3/27 profit JPY422.9bn annualises to ~JPY1.7tn): FY3/27 profit ~JPY1.48tn. BOJ continues to ~1.25-1.5%, deposit betas stay low, US IB reaches top-10 fee share and the fee/capital-light mix lifts ROE to ~14%, the level the 1.8x P/B currently prices. Japan's nominal growth settles at 2.5%.

bear.narrative: FY3/27 profit lands ~JPY1.32tn, below the raised guidance, then a US/global credit cycle and a BOJ pause/reversal compress NII, IB fees and trading while credit costs rise from today's low base: net revenue flat-to-down for two years and ROE back below 10%, i.e. Mizuho's pre-2024 history of earning roughly its cost of equity. Balance-sheet growth 3% falling to 1.5%; terminal growth 1.5% (Japan's pre-reflation nominal trend).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 default: profits have more than doubled in three years on BOJ normalisation and a benign credit cycle, the stock has nearly doubled in 52 weeks (US$6.09-11.49) to ~1.8x book, and the bear case (a return to Mizuho's long history of ROE at or below CoE) is a well-precedented outcome for this bank, not a tail.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Mizuho as a stream of distributable equity at a JPY cost of equity: what the bank can pay out after retaining enough capital to grow its risk-weighted assets. At steady state this reduces to P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g); the market's ~1.8x book prices a sustained ~14-15% ROE, our base ~12.5%.
key_risks_to_valuation: BOJ pause or reversal removes the NIM tailwind behind the guidance raises
US/global credit or IB-fee downturn hits the overseas CIB build
JGB portfolio mark-to-market if yields rise faster
Repeat of core-system failures and FSA action
Yen: a stronger yen lifts the USD value of the ADR but shrinks translated overseas earnings
J-GAAP FY0 profit inferred from guidance growth, not read from the Tanshin; CoE rests on an assumed JGB yield

data_sources.qualitative: MFG_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): FY3/27 guidance JPY1.40tn profit attributable, JPY1.75tn net business profit, MTP ROE >12% by FY3/29, JPY200bn buyback
